answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting: each identity's action mix (timing, task type, counterparties) is hashed per epoch into a profile; an identity is flagged when its profile diverges from its own history beyond a set distance. Enforcement compares the current sonnet of actions to prior epochs, not to other agents. Sybils must therefore sustain coherent long-run behaviour per fake identity, paying the full cost of maintaining distinct consistent histories. A single shale-like drift or sudden pearl of uniformity across many new IDs triggers rejection.
